description: Authoritative TS SDK public-surface inventory. Machine-readable, test-validated. Inventory is the source-of-truth for stability levels and change discipline; 007-CLIENT_SDK_GUIDE.md must stay aligned.

changeDisciplineValues.stable-deprecation-first: Breaking changes require a deprecation period. Removal only after at least one minor release with the deprecated API still available and a migration note in the migration ledger.
changeDisciplineValues.provisional-migration-required: Breaking changes are allowed but must be accompanied by a migration note in the migration ledger and a review-visible justification.
changeDisciplineValues.experimental-fast-break: Breaking changes are expected and may happen without prior deprecation. A brief note in the migration ledger is recommended but not enforced by the gate.

subpaths.note: Owns the current shared cancellation/resource-release baseline, the formal foundation-layer unified input-source helpers, the structured-observation baseline, replay signal primitive, shared authenticated-principal baseline, and the dual-layer error bridge: DisposableTrait, CancellationTokenTrait, CancellationTokenSourceTrait, createCancellationTokenSource(), and createLinkedCancellationToken() formalize cooperative cancellation plus owner-side release via dispose(); timer(), interval(), scheduleAt(), fromEventPattern(), fromSignal(), and fromPromise() are the current scheduler/input primitives above raw environment capabilities; ReadableReplaySignalTrait / WritableReplaySignalTrait / ComputedReplaySignalTrait, ReplaySignalSlot<T>, ReplaySignalWhenValueOptions, createReplaySignal(), createComputedReplaySignal(), createAndThenComputedReplaySignal(), readonlyReplaySignal(), and isReplaySignalTrait() formalize last-available channels that start empty, replay only emitted values, use get() for synchronous slot reads, and use cancellable whenValue() for asynchronous value waits; TraceEvent, TraceEventSinkTrait, createTraceTimelineStore() / TraceTimelineStore, createOperationTracer(), and OperationTraceEventType now formalize the machine-readable trace sink plus operation-correlation story; AuthenticatedPrincipal, normalizeAuthenticatedPrincipal(), normalizeAuthenticatedPrincipalWire(), and projectAuthenticatedPrincipal() now formalize the shared human-principal contract and host-facing projection baseline consumed by session/token-set families; ErrorPresentationDescriptor / ErrorPresentationTone / readErrorPresentationDescriptor(), ErrorAttributes, and describeError() remain the host-facing presentation, recovery, and structured error-attribute bridge built on runtime errors.

Owns the low-level persistence contracts used by browser login/callback flows, including the RecordStore atomic take capability and the keyed ephemeral flow-store helpers that formalise single-consume redirect state.

Owns browser-native interop for the foundation cancellation baseline through both bridge directions: createAbortSignalBridge(token) for fetch-facing consumers and createCancellationTokenFromAbortSignal(signal) for browser/framework consumers that receive AbortSignal first. It also owns the browser-layer unified input-source helpers fromAbortSignal(), fromStorageEvent(), and fromVisibilityChange(), higher-level lifecycle helpers such as createCrossTabSync() and createVisibilityReconciler(), and the foundation Web client-environment boundary: ClientEnvironmentPreset, WebClientEnvironment, PageClientEnvironment, createWebClientEnvironment(), createBrowserPageClientEnvironment(), createBrowserWorkerClientEnvironment(), createServiceWorkerClientEnvironment(), createBrowserExtensionBackgroundClientEnvironment(), requirePageClientEnvironment(), deriveClientEnvironment(), and ClientEnvironmentService. Canonical adopter-facing access is now the flattened environment shape (`environment.transport`, `environment.sessionStore`, and peers). ClientEnvironmentService is the reusable host-scoped layered resolver: resolve*() coalesces async materialization, read*() provides Suspense-compatible reads, and provider/injector scope owns lifecycle instead of JS module-cache singletons. These factories are explicit presets, not automatic host detection or a DI container.

Canonical owner of shared auth requirement orchestration primitives (RequirementPlanner, RouteRequirementOrchestrator). Consolidates the shared auth-coordination surface that was previously hosted under @securitydept/token-set-context-client/orchestration. Kind is an opaque string; each auth-context defines its own named constants.

Foundation event-stream contracts and RxJS-backed operator facade used by auth lifecycle telemetry. Exposes SecurityDept traits rather than requiring family packages to make RxJS their primary public contract.

Framework-neutral dependency injection authority. `SecuritydeptInjectorTrait` is the minimal read-side contract (`get()` only) shared by consumers, React Context, and adapter integrations; `SecuritydeptInjector` is the SDK facade that owns provider resolution, parent inheritance, explicit overrides, and side-effect-free `has()` checks without exposing raw injection-js runtime types as the canonical public shape. The subpath also re-exports typed `inject()` / `runInInjectionContext()` helpers and the Angular-style `SecuritydeptDestroyRef` lifecycle token for framework adapters such as React hosts.

Canonical framework-neutral RxJS bridge for SecurityDept event streams and signals. Exposes `toRxObservable(source)` for EventStreamTrait, ReadableSignalTrait, and ReadableReplaySignalTrait, plus `fromRxObservable(observable)` for the reverse bridge. Replay signals do not emit initial empty slots and replay only the last emitted value to late subscribers. `@securitydept/client/events` remains the event/operator surface; `@securitydept/client-angular` keeps Angular-native writable-signal bridging only.

Foundation shared structural utilities for SDK internals and advanced adapters. OnDemandTaskQueue owns the reusable async on-demand FIFO runner used by token-set auth-check scheduling so family packages do not reimplement queue fields, run-loop state, or pending-task rejection semantics.

Owns the raw Web router/security baseline. Navigation API first with History API + popstate fallback. Pre-commit intercept wires PlannerHost requirement evaluation into both backends so non-framework (Web Components / Lit / vanilla) adopters have a canonical router/security path aligned with Angular and TanStack Router.

Owns basic-auth browser/page redirect helpers. performRedirect() and loginWithRedirect() use an `environment` option carrying PageLocationCapability when provided and otherwise resolve the foundation page location capability; worker-like hosts must keep redirect initiation in a real page context or inject explicit page/navigation capability.

React entry is injector-first: it exports `BASIC_AUTH_CONTEXT_CLIENT`, `createBasicAuthContextClient()`, and `provideBasicAuthContextClient()` so hosts compose the client through `SecuritydeptProvider`. No domain-specific React Context, Provider component, or `useBasicAuthContext()` lookup hook remains in the public surface.

subpaths.note: Owns framework-neutral browser-shell convenience in core: rememberPostAuthRedirect(), clearPostAuthRedirect(), resolveLoginUrl(), and logoutAndClearPendingLoginRedirect(). The user-info principal contract aligns to the shared AuthenticatedPrincipal baseline from @securitydept/client, so stable subject/issuer/claims semantics no longer live in a narrower session-only owner. SessionContextController is the framework-neutral state owner for user-info refresh, logout cleanup, and redirect helpers; React and Angular adapters bridge this controller instead of owning parallel fetch state machines.

Owns session browser/page redirect helpers. loginWithRedirect() uses an `environment` option carrying PageLocationCapability when provided and otherwise resolves the foundation page location capability, keeping redirect initiation out of worker-like restore-only hosts.

React entry is injector-first and controller-bridged: it exports `SESSION_CONTEXT_CLIENT`, `SESSION_CONTEXT_CONTROLLER`, `createSessionContextController()`, and `provideSessionContextController()` so hosts compose session dependencies through `SecuritydeptProvider`. No `SessionContextProvider` or `useSessionContext()` public surface remains.

subpaths.note: Owns token-set backend-mode route/client contracts. Backend user-info transport remains a family DTO while its semantic authenticated-principal parsing/output aligns to the shared AuthenticatedPrincipal baseline from @securitydept/client instead of a parallel family-local owner.

Owns backend-OIDC browser-host helpers within the existing /web subpath. The canonical browser composition path is createBackendOidcModeWebClientEnvironment() first, then createBackendOidcModeWebClient({ environment, ...config }). Materialized backend web clients now expose the shared OIDC redirect-login surface loginWithRedirect({ environment, postAuthRedirectUri }); loginWithBackendOidcRedirect() remains the legacy/convenience alias. restoreBackendOidcModeClient() is worker-safe restore-only behavior; bootstrapBackendOidcModePageClient(), captureBackendOidcModePageCallbackFragment(), buildAuthorizeUrlReturningToCurrentPage(), currentPageLocationAsPostAuthRedirectUri(), loginWithBackendOidcPopup(), and relayBackendOidcPopupCallback() are page-boundary helpers. Page-oriented helpers now use options-object-first signatures with a typed `environment` field instead of positional page arguments or `pageEnvironment` option keys. Location-only helpers consume BackendOidcModePageLocationCapability; callback capture consumes BackendOidcModePageCallbackCapability; popup login consumes BackendOidcModePopupLoginCapability for callback-fragment storage; resetBackendOidcModeBrowserState() requires an explicit callbackFragmentStore and no longer constructs a global session-store-backed fragment store. No ./backend-oidc-mode/page subpath or deprecated aliases are part of this surface.

Includes the config projection source contract plus the current browser materialization owner: resolveConfigProjection(), networkConfigSource(), ConfigProjectionSourceKind, ClientReadinessState, createFrontendOidcModeWebClientEnvironment(), createFrontendOidcModeBrowserClient(), resolveFrontendOidcModePersistentStateKey(), and resolveFrontendOidcModeBrowserStorageKey(). The canonical browser composition path is createFrontendOidcModeWebClientEnvironment() first, then createFrontendOidcModeBrowserClient({ environment, ...projectionInput }); the materializer requires that explicit environment and does not create default store/fetch/origin dependency fallbacks. Async clientFactory support remains part of the browser contract. popupLogin() uses popupCallbackUrl as the real OAuth redirect_uri, supports an explicit postAuthRedirectUri for the opener, and is proven by the apps/webui reference host via popup relay plus cross-tab lifecycle browser e2e. FrontendOidcModeTraceEventType keeps popup / callback / refresh / user-info structured trace taxonomy shared and adopter-visible rather than app-local. describeFrontendOidcModeCallbackError() keeps callback-specific host-facing presentation/recovery mapping under the family owner while building on the shared client error presentation descriptor contract. Capability-first layering on the browser path keeps projection endpoint + redirectUri as bootstrap input, the resolved projection as auth-context config, and environment capability wiring explicit. Frontend-mode user-info and metadata principal construction aligns to the shared AuthenticatedPrincipal baseline, with app-facing display projection left to shared helper-backed host code.

Token-set-specific orchestration layer: auth-transport, base-client, controller, persistence, token-ops, types. RequirementPlanner and RouteRequirementOrchestrator are hosted by @securitydept/client/auth-coordination. AuthPrincipal aligns to the shared AuthenticatedPrincipal baseline while keeping resource-token facts and substrate ownership outside this human-principal contract.

Framework-neutral multi-client token-set auth registry core. Owns keyed storage, readiness tracking (not_initialized → initializing → ready | failed), canonical lifecycle verbs (`register(entry)`, `unregister(key)`, `resetMaterialization(key)`, `dispose()`), priority=primary|lazy lifecycle, preload / whenReady / idleWarmup, and the reactive registry topology/readiness authority through `state`. Omitted-key `whenReady()` and `clientSignalFor()` are single-registered-client conveniences; multi-client hosts must pass an explicit key. `whenReady()` waits for lazy materialization and registry-managed `client.start()` completion. `clientSignalFor(key?)` is the canonical reactive client acquisition API and triggers lazy materialization/start when called; the returned replay signal remains empty until a started client is ready. `registeredKeys()` / `readyKeys()` plus registered snapshot helpers are synchronous convenience over the registry state signal. `createTokenSetOidcAuthRegistry()` now uses the mode client itself as the materialized object; per-client auth state lives on OIDC mode client channels rather than on a service wrapper: replay signals for `authDetermined`, `authSnapshot`, `isAuthenticated`, and `authorizationHeaderValue`, plus plain signals for `lastAuthError` and `authOperations`. Advanced maintenance uses `client.authCheck(options)`; leaf consumers use replay signals instead of registry-level ensure sugar. The subpath also keeps multi-axis discrimination (urlPatterns, callbackPath, requirementKind, providerFamily), lifecycle-safe invalidation errors for stale async materialization, the shared managed OIDC client contracts (`OidcModeClient`, `OidcCallbackClient`), the shared generic callback failure presenter `describeTokenSetCallbackError()`, the callback resume error reader `readTokenSetCallbackResumeErrorDetails()`, and `TokenSetCallbackResumeController` as the shared callback resume state machine. Mode-specific callback copy remains an explicit override owned by the caller or mode package.

Token-set-specific raw web route helper that creates AuthGuardClientOption entries whose unauthenticated handler waits for the selected client's `isAuthenticated` replay signal before redirect/block fallback.

Owns focused test observation helpers for the current browser/SDK baseline: FakeClock, FakeScheduler, FakeTransport, and InMemoryTraceCollector. Operation-level trace observation through ofOperation(), operationLifecycle(), and assertOperationLifecycle() keeps tests from needing ad hoc operationId filters.

Angular entry keeps provideBasicAuthContext({ config }) as auth-context config only; Angular DI owns host registration, while the service facade stays a thin wrapper over core zone/redirect helpers. Angular DI is the composition root; service methods do not become a second foundation environment API.

subpaths.note: The Angular session adapter is environment-first at the composition root: provideSessionContext({ config, environment }) reads transport and sessionStore from one flattened WebClientEnvironment instead of exposing transport/sessionStore as the canonical provider shape. SessionContextService bridges SessionContextController, exposes state via Angular signal/Observable helpers, and makes initial user-info probing explicit through initialRefresh or service.refresh(). Low-level access still stays on SessionContextService.client; Angular DI remains the composition root and service methods consume the registered controller wiring instead of accepting a second foundation environment API.

subpaths.note: React token-set adapter is now injector-first. The root export owns explicit provider factories (`provideTokenSetAuthRegistry()`, `provideTokenSetCallbackResumeController()`), callback bridges (`useTokenSetCallbackResume()`, `TokenSetCallbackComponent`), and React-specific type re-exports on top of the framework-neutral registry core. Ordinary provider composition is scope-owned: `provide...` factories create registry/controller instances inside the current injection context and let `SecuritydeptDestroyRef` own teardown. Advanced hosts that need manual readiness, manual disposal, or custom warmup policy must create and own the registry/controller explicitly before value-providing them. Keyed auth state is read through `useSecuritydeptContext().get(TOKEN_SET_AUTH_REGISTRY)` plus `useReadableSignal(service.state)` or through explicit props; no `TokenSetAuthProvider`, fixed runtime bundle, hidden registry/service lookup hook, keyed state hook, or backend-client context helper remains in the public surface.

subpaths.note: Canonical token-set React Query integration surface (not a separate package). `@tanstack/react-query` is an optional peer dependency. This subpath owns cache-key namespacing, readiness queries over registry materialization, and namespace invalidation glue for token-set-aware consumers. Reference-app resource domain models, CRUD transport logic, and groups/entries mutations remain app-local or adopter-local code rather than SDK public surface.

Token-set-specific TanStack Router beforeLoad helper that wraps @securitydept/client-react/tanstack-router and waits for the selected client's `isAuthenticated` replay signal for each route requirement before redirect/block fallback.

Root export owns TokenSetAuthRegistry DI service, multi-client integration, bearer interceptor (BearerInterceptorOptions { strictUrlMatch?: boolean } + TOKEN_SET_BEARER_INTERCEPTOR_OPTIONS InjectionToken; provideTokenSetBearerInterceptor(options?) and createTokenSetBearerInterceptor(registry, options?) accept the same options object — strictUrlMatch: true bounds bearer injection to URLs matching registered urlPatterns), callback resume, and the canonical Angular route-security builders. TokenSetAuthRegistry is now a thin DI wrapper over the shared `createTokenSetOidcAuthRegistry()` lifecycle owner and exposes the same canonical verbs plus signal-state authority as the core: `register(entry)`, `unregister(key)`, `resetMaterialization(key)`, `dispose()`, `state`, registered snapshots, ready keys, and `clientSignalFor()`. Registry methods materialize and return mode clients; Angular-specific code should bridge client replay signals (`authSnapshot`, `isAuthenticated`, `authorizationHeaderValue`, `authOperations`) with `@securitydept/client/rx` or `bridgeToAngularSignal()` when needed rather than using a per-client service wrapper. secureRouteRoot() / secureRoute() are the adopter-facing Angular Router path: child routes declare serializable requirement metadata only, root registers non-serializable runtime policy (planner hosts, requirementPolicies, handlers), and both canActivate + canActivateChild evaluate the full route chain in one pass. createTokenSetRouteAggregationGuard() remains the lower-level route-tree primitive and passes attemptedUrl from Angular router state rather than from page globals. createTokenSetOidcLoginRedirectHandler() is the page redirect helper layered on top of that route context, targeting the shared OidcRedirectLoginClient contract. Its public key remains `environment`, and the canonical path is providePageClientEnvironment({ environment }) from @securitydept/client-angular. The helper awaits that source inside the guard flow before calling `loginWithRedirect()`. CallbackResumeService now bridges TokenSetCallbackResumeController and exposes component-free resume(url) state through Angular signals / observables; the canonical signal/event-to-RxJS bridge now lives in `@securitydept/client/rx`, while `@securitydept/client-angular` keeps Angular-specific writable-signal bridging.

Shared React framework bridge with the only SDK-owned React Context. Root exports include `SecuritydeptContext`, `SecuritydeptProvider`, and `useSecuritydeptContext()` for injector access, the context-free signal/event bridge `useReadableSignal()` and `useEventStream()`, and shared dependency tokens/provider factories such as `CLIENT_ENVIRONMENT_SERVICE` / `provideClientEnvironmentService()` and `AUTH_PLANNER_HOST` / `provideAuthPlannerHost()`. Domain packages compose through this injector bridge instead of publishing additional React Context/Provider APIs.

subpaths.note: Canonical owner of TanStack React Router route-security contract, aligned with Angular's @securitydept/client-angular route metadata contract. Canonical adopter-facing entry: createSecureBeforeLoad() — a beforeLoad-compatible factory that wires root-level runtime policy into TanStack Router execution semantics (throws redirect or RouteSecurityBlockedError). Child routes use withTanStackRouteRequirements() for serializable staticData declaration only. Lower-level building blocks: extractTanStackRouteRequirements (full-route aggregation with merge/replace/inherit), createTanStackRouteSecurityPolicy (headless evaluator), projectTanStackRouteMatches, createTanStackRouteActivator.

Canonical owner of Angular framework bridge utilities. Provides: AuthRouteAdapter (projection from ActivatedRouteSnapshot to RouteMatchNode[]), PlannerHost DI wiring (provideAuthPlannerHost, AUTH_PLANNER_HOST, injectPlannerHost), route-metadata helpers (withRouteRequirements, extractFullRouteRequirements, ROUTE_REQUIREMENTS_DATA_KEY, ROUTE_REQUIREMENTS_COMPOSITION_DATA_KEY, resolveEffectiveRequirements), canonical page-environment DI bridge utilities (providePageClientEnvironment, PAGE_CLIENT_ENVIRONMENT, PageClientEnvironmentService, PageClientEnvironmentResolver, PageClientEnvironmentSource), the Angular writable-signal bridge `bridgeToAngularSignal()`, and provideRouteScopedRequirements (lower-level non-router DI-scope helper). Framework-neutral RxJS bridging for ReadableSignalTrait/EventStreamTrait now lives in `@securitydept/client/rx`, so `@securitydept/client-angular` no longer owns a generic `signalToObservable()` public API. ReadableSignalTrait from @securitydept/client remains the canonical signal contract.
